title: Ignore bytecode and temp files in local plugin watcher

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The unanchored __pycache__ check silences legitimate plugin trees
leads.consequence: An installed plugin whose valid directory/ID contains __pycache__, e.g. acme.__pycache__widget, is discovered and can be enabled, but editing even its Widget.qml or manifest.json emits no localPluginChanged. The POSIX --exclude matches the full path and the JS guard also matches the whole relative path. A HOME path containing the token suppresses all watcher output, even for ordinary plugin IDs. Changes only take effect on a manual rescan/shell restart. Match a path component equal to __pycache__ (and account for the home prefix) rather than any substring.
leads.triage: confirmed (validator regex, Sol sealed run, Opus self-check runs review-plan-4); published as finding

leads.summary: Non-bytecode runtime files remain capable of a reload loop
leads.consequence: The new denylist does not exclude files written as runtime state, such as data.json. If an enabled local plugin writes data.json during initialization, inotifywait reports CREATE/CLOSE_WRITE, the path resolver returns the plugin ID, and shell.qml restarts the reload timer; that reload can start the writer again. The PR addresses Python caches but does not solve this adjacent path of the same failure mode. Open PR #12189 deliberately chooses an allowlist to handle such state files, so the two approaches need an explicit scope decision.
leads.triage: pre-existing scope (#12158), not a regression; dropped

leads.summary: Related open watcher-filter PRs require a conscious conflict resolution
leads.consequence: Open, diverged #12189 adds --include at exactly this command and a new JS allowlist; git merge-file of its own change against #12020 has conflict markers in both watcher and classifier. If a resolution simply retains both --include and --exclude arguments, inotifywait 4.25.9.0 rejects them with 'include and exclude regexp cannot both be specified.', exits before watching, and the existing 1s restart timer repeats the failure. Open, diverged #10705 adds a different --exclude at the same line, also a conflict; retaining two separate --exclude flags silently uses the last, so one PR's rules are lost. Resolve to one coherent filter and matching JS predicate if either merges, do not concatenate flags.
leads.triage: already in Opus final; corroborated; published

leads.summary: The existing registry fixture does not cover either new ignore rule
leads.consequence: The four existing watcher assertions cover QML edits, .git and hidden staging, but none calls localPluginIdForPath with __pycache__, .pyc, an atomic .pyc.<id>, or a temp file, nor does a test exercise inotifywait's exclusion. A plausible regression deleting both newly added guards and the --exclude lines passes every existing fixture assertion. The contract test also exits successfully without running any assertions when there is no compositor. Add negative cache/temp paths and at least one positive legitimate sibling / real watcher assertion before treating 'plugins-test passes' as coverage of this change.
leads.triage: already in Opus final; corroborated; published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: Four shipped plugin-author guides still promise reloads on every file save
leads.consequence: All four guides promise that saving a file anywhere in an installed plugin reloads code, whereas the new watcher explicitly suppresses .tmp, .bak, .swp, .swx and cache paths, and a __pycache__ substring in a plugin ID suppresses even manifest and QML saves. Plugin authors following the blanket promise can mistakenly expect automatic refresh when editing these paths. Qualify the descriptions to name the files now excluded and describe manual rescan when appropriate.
leads.triage: text verified at 4 locations; judged minor nitpick; not published

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change removes the reload triggers behind #11929. In live `inotifywait` runs with inotify-tools 4.25.9.0 and Python 3.14.7 (the versions in the issue), CPython's bytecode writes stopped producing a plugin id, while edits to plugin sources still did. Below: a conflict with two open PRs that edit the same watcher arguments, a side effect of the suffix patterns in `--exclude`, an over-broad `__pycache__` match, and a test note.

| Step (synthetic plugin tree) | Base: lines mapped to a plugin id | Head |
|---|---|---|
| First import (creates `__pycache__`, temp `.pyc.<id>`, final `.pyc`) | 14 | 0 (2 directory lines printed, dropped by the JS filter) |
| Recompile into an existing `__pycache__` | 20 | 0 |
| `python -O` import (`.opt-1.pyc`) | 20 | 0 |
| Delete `__pycache__` | 5 | 0 |

**Verified:** writing QML files, `manifest.json` and `.py` files, a vim writebackup save, an atomic save via `Service.qml.tmp` renamed into place, a new directory with files, and a plugin moved into place from `.add.tmp.<pid>` all still produce a plugin id on the head.

### Open PRs #12189 and #10705 edit the same `inotifywait` arguments

Both PRs insert an option at the same place in `localPluginWatcher.command`, and both conflict textually with this PR. Keeping both options when resolving the conflict causes a different problem for each (checked with inotify-tools 4.25.9.0):

| PR | Adds | If combined with this PR's `--exclude` |
|---|---|---|
| #12189 | `--include "(manifest\\.json$\|\\.manifest\\.json$\|\\.(qml\|js)$)"` plus an allowlist in `localPluginIdForPath` | `inotifywait` exits 1 with `include and exclude regexp cannot both be specified.`; `onExited` restarts it every second and no events arrive, so hot reload stops |
| #10705 | a second `--exclude` (`.git`, `__pycache__`, `node_modules`) | only the last `--exclude` applies; the warning goes to stderr, which the shell discards |

**Impact:** whichever PR merges second can silently disable hot reload (#12189) or drop one of the two filters (#10705) if the conflict is resolved by keeping both lines.

**Suggested change:** coordinate on a single filter. #12189's allowlist also stops the `__pycache__` reloads on its own, so if it lands, this PR's `--exclude` would need to go.

### Suffix patterns in `--exclude` leave stale paths after a directory rename

libinotifytools applies `--exclude` before `inotifywait` updates its watch names for renames. When a directory is renamed away from an excluded name (`*.tmp`, `*.bak`, `*~`), the filtered `MOVED_FROM` never updates the name, and later events inside that directory are reported under the old path:

```text
mv acme.helper/assets.tmp acme.helper/assets
new file acme.helper/assets/b.svg
  base: acme.helper/assets/b.svg
  head: acme.helper/assets.tmp/b.svg        (stale name, still reloads: id comes from the first segment)

mv .delta.tmp delta                          (top-level hidden staging name)
edit delta/Widget.qml
  base: delta/Widget.qml         -> reload
  head: .delta.tmp/Widget.qml    -> dropped by the existing hidden-entry check, no reload
```

**Impact:** a plugin moved into place from a hidden `.tmp`, `.bak` or `~` staging directory stops hot-reloading until the watcher restarts. Omarchy's own staging and backup names (`.add.tmp.<pid>`, `.clone.XXXXXX`, `.<id>.bak.<timestamp>`) do not match the patterns, so only manual or third-party flows are affected.

**Suggested change:** keep only names that are never renamed into place in `--exclude`, for example `(/__pycache__(/|$)|/\.git/)` (argv form; not run through `inotifywait`), and leave the suffix patterns to the JS filter in `localPluginIdForPath`. In the same runs, the JS filter alone suppressed the artefacts just as well: 21 triggers against 21 in the bytecode and editor run, and 8 against 6 in the rename run, where the 2 extra are the real `delta/Widget.qml` edits that the head drops.

### Unanchored `__pycache__` match suppresses plugins whose id contains it

`__pycache__` is matched as an unanchored substring in both the regex and `relative.indexOf("__pycache__")`. `bin/omarchy-plugin-validate` accepts ids with underscores, so a plugin id such as `acme.__pycache__widget` is valid. In sandbox runs, edits to that plugin's `manifest.json` and `Widget.qml` printed nothing on the head, while the base mapped each to the plugin id.

**Impact:** such a plugin gets no hot reloads at all. Installs are still picked up, because `omarchy plugin add` runs an explicit rescan.

**Suggested change:** match `__pycache__` only as a whole path component in both places, for example the regex above (argv form; not run through `inotifywait`) plus `("/" + relative + "/").indexOf("/__pycache__/") !== -1` in the JS check.

**Optional test improvement:** the JS filter carries real load. On inotify-tools 4.25.9.0, recursive mode skips the `--exclude` regex for directory `CREATE`/`MOVED_TO` events, so each new `__pycache__` directory is still printed and only the new `localPluginIdForPath` line drops it. The four existing `localPluginIdForPath` assertions in `test/shell.d/fixtures/plugin-registry/shell.qml` do not cover any of the new paths, and `plugins-test.sh` (cited in the PR) validates manifests and a few `shell.qml` patterns, none of which touch the watcher. Cases such as `__pycache__/x.cpython-314.pyc`, the temp name `__pycache__/x.cpython-314.pyc.1234`, a bare `.../__pycache__` directory path, `Widget.qml~`, `.Widget.qml.swp`, plus a positive `helper/x.py`, would catch a later removal of that line.
